title: Writing a Buffered Tape Symbol
statement: Let $x,w$ be Boolean words, let $d$ be a one-work-tape configuration on input $x$, let $r$ be a natural number with $r<|w|$, and choose phases $s,s'$, an input-head position $ip$, and a sign $m\in\{-1,0,1\}$. If the machine’s transition at phase $s$, when given the input and work-tape symbols in the configuration with $w$ buffered through its first $r$ symbols and the work head at offset $r$, is the action that writes the $r$-th symbol of $w$ on that tape, moves its head by $m$, leaves the input head still, produces no output, and enters phase $s'$, then one machine step yields the configuration with the first $r+1$ symbols of $w$ buffered, phase $s'$, unchanged input-head position, and work-head displacement $r+m$ from its original position.
hypotheses_covered: transition at the specified configuration equals the stated write-and-move action
